description:
Residual of the native re-green, split out of fz-go4.18.3. The keystone (fz-go4.18.3.1) de-coupled the resume-PAYLOAD shape from oscillating demand and greened 2 of 8. The remaining 6 fail at a SEPARATE convergence locus: the transport INPUT-merge / executable-MEMBERSHIP demand path, schedule-dependent non-monotonicity.

REMAINING FAILURES (at HEAD after keystone lands; 931/6)
- compiler2_native_program_adapts_delivered_calls_from_callee_return_lanes -> "native clause dispatch required omitted semantic input 1 for executable 185" (a transport INPUT shape erased, not a resume).
- compiler2_native_program_carries_published_callable_boundary_targets_into_closure_calls -> same "omitted semantic input" family.
- compiler2_native_program_jit_adapts_callable_raw_returns_back_to_value_refs -> "materialize absent value ty Ty(21) in Continuation{FnId(7), index 2}".
- compiler2_native_program_resource_fixture_shapes_callable_boundaries_explicitly -> test assertion "resource return is not transported".
- compiler2_native_program_does_not_fabricate_nil_for_zero_width_resume_payloads -> no retained zero-width continuation.
- escaping_destructor_keys_its_activation_at_the_grounded_boundary_surface -> PoisonError, full-run only = schedule-dependent.

EVIDENCE IT IS A DISTINCT LOCUS
Between two identical single-test runs the fatal SHIFTS ("missing return-flow position ExecutableReturn{...,need:Value}" <-> "omitted semantic input 1"), confirming schedule-dependent demand/membership non-monotonicity. The "missing ExecutableReturn position" is a MEMBERSHIP gap (executable/frontier flicker), not a shape gap.

SEARCH NARROWED (two loci ruled out — do NOT repeat)
- NOT record_return_demand (already monotone via join_assign).
- NOT the RuntimeDemand product reads: a monotone ExecutableRuntimeDemand::raise_to_floor (sound — derive_executable_runtime_demand reads only a target's input_demands, never callable_flows, at runtime_demand.rs:2147/2355/2485) + monotone record_latest_runtime_demand + flooring every demand read was built clean with NO regressions but was COMPLETELY INERT for the 6. The residual shrink does not flow through RuntimeDemand product reads.
- A cycle-seed floor at produce_runtime_demand_product was also inert (and a naive version regressed range_and_map_to_list by changing wait-vs-proceed flow).

LIKELY TRUE LOCUS
collect_executable_input_constraints (transport.rs:2796) — its own comment documents a known schedule-dependent non-monotone anchor/union gate — plus the demanded-executable frontier / executable-membership flicker. Fix must be correct-by-construction and PROVEN monotone (schedule-independence test, repeated/varied-order full runs), not green-once. Apply the same producer-sourced / monotone-join discipline as the keystone to the input-merge path.

SIGNAL
cargo test --lib compiler2 = 0 failed, STABLE across >=3 fresh full runs and schedule-varied drives. Then fz-go4.18.3 (umbrella) is satisfied and fz-go4.18.4 (delete spine) unblocks.

comments.text: Lead (unverified): during fz-go4.18.3.1 a MORE AGGRESSIVE variant was explored but NOT committed (it leaked into the main checkout as uncommitted changes; saved at scratchpad/stray-aggressive-resume.diff). It drops the !demand.is_callable() gate entirely and unions EVERY resume that has a local callee return position (callable returns included) with the callee ExecutableReturn, plus a debug eprintln. The keystone deliberately kept callable returns on the demand-driven path to preserve boundary selection. Whether producer-sourcing callable resume returns helps the residual 6 is UNPROVEN (the residual signatures are input-merge/membership 'omitted semantic input' + 'missing ExecutableReturn position', not resume-callable). Treat only as a possible angle; the prime suspect remains collect_executable_input_constraints (transport.rs:2796) + the demanded-executable frontier.

title: Transport input-merge / executable-membership demand monotonicity (re-green remaining 6 native tests)
